item: CONFIRMED 19 AUG 2026 AGAINST A REAL DATABASE: one household's upsert overwrites another household's plaid_items row. Acting as household A with marginsheet.household_id set to A, verified by reading current_setting back inside the transaction, the statement exchange.ts issues (`insert into plaid_items ... on conflict (item_id) do update set access_token_ciphertext = excluded...`) SUCCEEDED against a row owned by household B and replaced B's access_token_ciphertext. Ownership stayed with B only because household_id is not in the SET list. household_isolation did not refuse it. THE ROUTE IS ORDINARY USE, NOT AN ATTACK: item_id is Plaid's, and two households linking THE SAME joint account produce the same item_id, so this arrives through a shared bank login rather than through a guessed UUID. Consequences: B's Plaid token is destroyed so B's syncs break, and B's row then holds a token minted for A, which is a cross-household data path into B's ledger the next time sync runs. The same shape applies to financial_accounts.plaid_account_id, which carries the same global unique index; that half is NOT yet proven, because the test exercising it had a NOT NULL omission that made it pass vacuously. NOT FIXED IN THE CURRENT CHAIN, by Guy's ruling: it is a schema-level finding whose fix touches migrations, the exchange path and the account-overlap item, and it needs its own plan rather than being folded into a PR about something else. The proving test and its register entry are preserved on branch finding/cross-household-upsert; they were removed from the authorization PR because the finding is real and would otherwise hold a live security fix behind a red check.

item: EVERY OUTBOUND CALL A LOCKED SYNC MAKES RUNS UNDER AN AbortSignal DEADLINE (Guy, 19 Aug 2026, rejecting both options offered). A LOCK TIMEOUT IS ALWAYS A LIE: it asserts the holder is dead without knowing, and if the holder is alive it hands out the exact concurrency the lock exists to prevent. Failing the waiter is the honest version of the same non-answer, converting a stuck household into an erroring one without ever ending the thing that is stuck. Bounding the OPERATION means the task always settles, the lock releases in its existing `finally` with no special path, there is never a second writer, and nothing has to decide whether a holder is dead because it made it true instead of assuming it. THE TRAP, and the reason this needs a planted mutation: Promise.race against a timer IS NOT A TIMEOUT. It stops waiting, not working; the hung call keeps running and can still write, so a raced deadline is the release-the-lock horn wearing better clothes and it reads as correct in review. The planted mutation replaces the abort with a race and a test must tell them apart; if nothing reddens, the control cannot distinguish a safe timeout from an unsafe one. THE FINDING TO RECORD RATHER THAN LEAVE IN THE IMPLEMENTATION: a deadline is only safe if every operation under it is genuinely abortable.

WHAT HAPPENS OTHERWISE: each sweep adds a waiter behind a task that is not progressing rather than replacing it, so the watchdog grows the queue it exists to drain, and the state machine reports recovery throughout. A FAILURE THAT AMPLIFIES ITSELF IS A DIFFERENT SEVERITY FROM ONE THAT PERSISTS. See [bound-the-work-not-the-lock] for the other half, which is genuinely separate: bounding the work means the deadline handles hung work inside a live object and the watchdog handles an object that DIED. Two conditions, two mechanisms, no shared clock, nothing to drift, which dissolves the one-clock concern that was raised against a lock timeout.

item: RULED 20 AUG 2026 (Guy): INVESTMENT ACCOUNTS ARE VISIBLE AS ACCOUNTS AND EXCLUDED FROM THE SPENDING LEDGER. Arrived by default rather than by ruling: SoFi's first connection brought two investment accounts into financial_accounts, and the sync writes transactions against any account it holds. THE REASONING IS ALREADY DOCTRINE RATHER THAN NEW. A transfer to a brokerage is a DEPLOYMENT, not spending: money moving from cash to net worth, which the two-ledger rule already covers. A stock purchase INSIDE a brokerage is not a household transaction at all, it is an account rebalancing itself. Counting either as spending makes Kept wrong IN THE DIRECTION THAT PUNISHES EXACTLY THE BEHAVIOUR THE METHOD EXISTS TO ENCOURAGE. WHAT THIS MEANS: investment accounts appear in the accounts list and on the Balance Sheet at M8, and their transactions never enter the P&L. The transfer that funds them is already handled, because a transfer is not spending and deployment attribution is what it becomes. WHAT THE ADVICE GATE DOES NOT COVER: it refuses investment QUESTIONS and does not stop investment TRANSACTIONS being counted as spending. The harm is in the ledger, not in the replies. TWO THINGS TO SETTLE RATHER THAN ASSUME. (1) WHETHER INVESTMENT TRANSACTIONS ARE STORED AT ALL, or fetched and discarded. Guy's lean is STORE THEM, FLAGGED, EXCLUDED FROM THE LEDGER, the same shape as removed transactions which are flagged rather than deleted: storing costs nothing and gives a future Balance Sheet history, while discarding means M8 backfills. (2) WHAT HAPPENS TO THE ACCOUNT BALANCE. It is the number a household would actually want on a Balance Sheet, and it is NET-WORTH-SHAPED, so the net worth doctrine governs HOW IT RENDERS rather than whether it is held: never a hero metric, never celebrated, reported as position rather than scored. ESTABLISHED 21 AUG 2026, AND IT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN AN OBSERVATION. Guy confirmed both accounts hold real money in SoFi. We report 0.00 for both. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: WE DO NOT HOLD A TRUSTWORTHY INVESTMENT BALANCE, and that does not depend on why. The leading explanation is that Plaid withholds investment balances without the Investments product, which fits everything seen, and it is a MECHANISM rather than a verified cause; the consequence is identical under any explanation, so the action does not wait on confirming it. Note the value is 0.00 and not null: exchange.ts writes balances.current ?? null, so Plaid sent a zero rather than omitting the field, which is why nothing looked wrong. CONSEQUENCE ONE: INVESTMENT ACCOUNTS MUST NOT RENDER A BALANCE UNTIL WE HOLD A REAL ONE. A 0.00 we cannot substantiate is worse than omitting the account, because A ZERO IS A CLAIM AND AN ABSENCE IS NOT. It is the fifth instance today of a number that reads as an answer and is not one, after oldestInWindow reporting the newest date, an empty account list reading as nothing connected, a milestone already set reading as not-yet-due, and a gate that could only refuse reading as caution. The rendering rule is the same each time: show nothing, or show why, but never show a figure the data does not support. CONSEQUENCE TWO: THE INVESTMENTS DECISION IS SHARPER THAN IT WAS WRITTEN. This item previously read as add Investments for holdings and cost basis, a richer view on top of a working balance. That is wrong. INVESTMENTS IS REQUIRED FOR ANY INVESTMENT FIGURE AT ALL. The post-launch portfolio view, you have $X, contributed $Y, grew $Z, needs the product for even the FIRST figure, and balance snapshots do not give it to us because the snapshots are the thing reading zero. So M8's Balance Sheet either omits investment balances entirely or waits on the product; there is no version that shows a number today. AND THE RESEARCH THAT PRECEDED THIS OBSERVATION REACHED THE OPPOSITE CONCLUSION, WHICH IS WHY BOTH ARE KEPT. A branch opened before the SoFi connection concluded, correctly from the documentation, that Plaid's `current` for an investment account is 'the total value of assets as presented by the institution' and `available` is 'the total cash available to withdraw', and therefore that $X invested was already obtainable from the balance without the Investments product. PRODUCTION SAYS OTHERWISE: both accounts report 0.00 while holding real money. The documentation describes what those fields MEAN, not whether they are populated for an Item that never consented to Investments, and the two are different questions. This is the same shape as every other finding of 20 and 21 Aug: a true statement about a mechanism extended to a claim about a case nobody had observed. The research is preserved below because its OTHER conclusions still stand and were confirmed rather than contradicted. --- RESEARCH, AS WRITTEN BEFORE THE OBSERVATION: RULED 20 AUG 2026 (Guy), AMENDED THE SAME DAY, AND ONE HALF OF THE ORIGINAL FRAMING WAS WRONG. CORRECTION FIRST, because a later reader would otherwise assume a live problem was fixed: THE ORIGINAL ITEM SAID INVESTMENT TRANSACTIONS WOULD LAND IN THE SPENDING LEDGER. THEY WOULD NOT. Plaid's docs are explicit that /investments/transactions/get 'can only be used for investment-type accounts; for obtaining transaction history for other account types, use Transactions', so the Transactions product cannot retrieve investment account history at all. With Investments not in our products array there is almost certainly NOTHING ARRIVING TO EXCLUDE. THE EXCLUSION RULE STANDS AND IS BUILT AS A GUARD AGAINST A FUTURE STATE rather than a fix for a live one. THE RULING, UNCHANGED: investment transactions never enter the spending ledger. A transfer to a brokerage is a DEPLOYMENT, not spending, which the two-ledger rule already covers; a stock purchase inside a brokerage is an account rebalancing itself and is not a household transaction. Counting either as spending makes Kept wrong IN THE DIRECTION THAT PUNISHES EXACTLY THE BEHAVIOUR THE METHOD EXISTS TO ENCOURAGE. THE STORAGE QUESTION IS RULED RATHER THAN LEANED: STORE THEM, FLAGGED, EXCLUDED FROM THE P&L, the same shape as removed transactions which are flagged rather than deleted. The data is kept DELIBERATELY, because a consolidated portfolio view is a post-launch product decision Guy has now made: not advice and not recommendations, just facts. You have $X invested, you contributed $Y, it grew $Z. Contributions are deployment, growth is arithmetic on balances, and neither recommends anything. WHAT WE ACTUALLY HAVE TODAY, established against the docs rather than assumed: ACCOUNTS AND BALANCES ONLY. No holdings, no cost basis, no positions, no securities, no buy or sell history. The balance is more useful than expected: for an investment account Plaid's `current` is 'the total value of assets as presented by the institution', so it is market value, and `available` is 'the total cash available to withdraw', so cash versus invested is visible. `limit` is null. So $X invested comes from `current`, $Z grew is arithmetic across account_balance_snapshots, and $Y contributed is inferable ONLY FROM THE FUNDING SIDE. THAT LIMIT IS THE SHAPE RATHER THAN A GAP: growth-versus-contribution decomposition is only as complete as the accounts connected, so a contribution from an account we do not hold is invisible. That is a property of connecting accounts and not something to fix. THE BALANCE RENDERS UNDER THE NET WORTH DOCTRINE: never a hero metric, never celebrated, reported as position rather than scored.

item: CONFIRMED AGAINST PLAID'S DOCS 20 AUG 2026, NOT RECALLED. transactions.days_requested appears nowhere in this repository. So every Item we have ever created holds 90 days of history, on every institution, because of a field we never sent. TWO CONSEQUENCES, AND THEY NEED DIFFERENT ACTIONS. (1) FOR FUTURE CONNECTIONS the fix is one field on the link token: transactions: { days_requested: 730 }. Authorised by Guy 20 Aug 2026 as a live defect independent of what caused the 201, and sequenced after PR 128 lands and the readout runs. (2) FOR THE ITEMS THAT ALREADY EXIST THERE IS NO CHEAP FIX. Plaid's API reference: 'Once Transactions has been added to an Item, this value cannot be updated.' The field applies only where the Transactions product has NOT already been initialised, so LINK UPDATE MODE DOES NOT HELP: extending history on an initialised Item requires /item/remove followed by sending the household through Link to create a NEW Item. That is a new item_id, a re-consent, and the duplicate-account path Guy already ruled on in the Option A overlap decision. It is a household-visible action, so it is a ruling rather than a maintenance step. WHAT IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED: whether the 90-day default is what produced 201 on SoFi. That is a mechanism rather than a diagnosis until the ledger readout reports the oldest transaction date; roughly 90 days ago is the signature, and 24 months falsifies it. THE FINDING THIS REPLACED is the one worth remembering: a projection-spec finding blaming two institutions for a uniform window was about to be written, when the window was uniform because we asked all of them the same question. Recorded in CLAUDE.md as its own species. TWO RULINGS, GUY, 20 AUG 2026, BOTH TAKEN BEFORE THE READOUT BECAUSE BOTH ARE CHEAPER NOW. (A) NO FURTHER INSTITUTIONS ARE CONNECTED UNTIL days_requested IS ON THE LINK TOKEN. Chase and Amex were next and would each connect at 90 days and each need the same destroy-and-recreate. One Item to redo is a nuisance; three is a pattern we chose. (B) IF THE READOUT CONFIRMS 90 DAYS ON SOFI, THE ITEM IS REMOVED AND RECONNECTED BEFORE ANYTHING BUILDS ON IT. The 201 rows are worth nothing as a ledger: M5 would categorise 90 days of history as though it were the household's record, and the census reads seasonal shape from a window that does not have any. item: THE CLASS RATHER THAN THE INSTANCE (Guy, 20 Aug 2026). THE FAILURE MODE OF HOUSEHOLD ISOLATION, WHEN MISCONFIGURED, IS AN EMPTY RESULT. Not an error, not a refusal: silence, which is indistinguishable from a household that genuinely has nothing. household_isolation reads current_setting('marginsheet.household_id', true), whose missing_ok argument returns NULL rather than raising, so an unset GUC evaluates household_id = NULL, matches no row, and raises nothing at all. EVERY RLS-SCOPED READ IN THIS SYSTEM HAS THAT SHAPE, so a broken GUC anywhere presents as a customer with no data rather than as a fault. PAID FOR ON 20 AUG 2026, TWICE, IN PRODUCTION, SILENTLY. /plaid/accounts answered an empty account list for every household, and the connect page showed 'none yet' for hours while SoFi was connected; Guy read that as a page not yet wired rather than as a symptom, which is exactly the ambiguity. The invitation actor lookup refused every actor with no_member. Neither raised anything and neither reached Sentry. Both shipped. THE PROPOSAL, NOT YET RULED ON: any read whose empty result would be a plausible business answer should ASSERT THE GUC IS SET rather than merely rely on it. A household with no accounts and a household whose GUC never survived are the same JSON, and only the reader can tell them apart today. Candidate shapes: a helper that reads current_setting and throws when it is null before the query runs, or a per-statement assertion, or an invariant test per RLS-scoped route. WHAT IS ALREADY DONE AND IS NOT THIS: a receiver scan requires every set_config to sit on a transaction handle, and a db test demonstrates the GUC dying outside one. Those stop the specific mistake. They do not make an empty result self-describing, which is what this item is about. AND THE SMALL SHARP THING WORTH KEEPING: phone-change.ts explained is_local correctly, in a comment, while three other call sites got it wrong. A comment is the weakest form of a rule, paid for again.
trigger: before M8 renders any household-facing list from an RLS-scoped read, because that is the point at which an empty result stops being a developer reading JSON and becomes a household being told they have nothing

item: CONFIRMED BY READING THE CODE, 20 AUG 2026, BEFORE ANY RECONNECT COULD HIDE IT (Guy). NOTHING REFRESHES A BALANCE AFTER CONNECTION. Three facts, each checked: (1) account_balance_snapshots is written in exactly ONE place, services/sync/src/exchange.ts, at token exchange. (2) financial_accounts.current_balance and available_balance are written in that same one place. (3) transactions-sync.ts DOES NOT EVEN DECLARE an accounts field on SyncPage, so the balances Plaid returns with EVERY /transactions/sync page are discarded at the type boundary and no code ever reads them. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE ONE GUY NAMED: Cash Flow would project a 13 week path from a number that never moves, and a household's balance would read as current while being weeks or months old. It is the same shape as the paginator counting rows and throwing them away, recorded in 4.5b prime: the data arrives, is counted or typed past, and is never written. WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: a balance renders identically whether it is live or frozen. There is no error, no empty result and no missing field, which is the same silence the RLS class already documents, arriving in a value rather than in a row count. THE READOUT NOW REPORTS IT: current and available balance, the account row's updated_at, and the count plus oldest and newest date of that account's snapshots, so live and stale are distinguishable by looking rather than by reasoning. WHAT IS OWED AND NOT YET RULED: where the refresh belongs. The cheap option is that the sync runner reads page.accounts from /transactions/sync, which arrives free with every page and needs no extra Plaid call. The alternative is /accounts/balance/get, which is a billed call and returns a FRESH balance rather than a cached one, and the difference matters for an available balance that a household is about to spend against. There is also a question of whether a snapshot is written per sync or per day, since account_balance_snapshots is keyed by date and the projection reads a series rather than a point. THE DATA IS ALREADY IN MEMORY, WHICH CHANGES WHAT THE FIX COSTS. callPlaid returns the WHOLE parsed body cast to its type parameter (plaid-client.ts): a cast is not a filter, so page.accounts and its balances are present at runtime on every /transactions/sync page. Nothing fetches them because nothing READS them, and the SyncPage interface omitting the field is the only reason nobody noticed. The fix is reading what we hold, not making a call. BILLING, FROM GUY 20 AUG 2026: the balances in sync pages are FREE, included in the Transactions subscription already paid per Item per month. /accounts/balance/get is BILLED PER CALL and forces a live institution refresh. /accounts/get is free but cached. So discarding the sync-page balances means choosing between stale balances and paying per call for something we were already handed. WHICH PRODUCT CASH FLOW ACTUALLY NEEDS, and Guy's reasoning is the ruling rather than a lean: a 13 week projection wants a balance that MOVES WITH THE SYNC, not a live one, because the projection is a path computed from a ledger and a balance fetched at a different instant than the transactions would disagree with them. So the free path is the right one for Cash Flow, and /accounts/balance/get is reserved for the household asking WILL THIS CLEAR RIGHT NOW, which is a different question with a different freshness requirement and a per-call cost that is justified by being asked. BUILT 21 AUG 2026, to the ruling. applyBalances reads page.accounts from every /transactions/sync page, writes current, available and limit onto financial_accounts scoped by household AND plaid_account_id, and upserts today's snapshot on (account_id, date) with the last write winning. SyncPage now DECLARES the accounts field, which is the whole of why the data was invisible: callPlaid returns the parsed body cast to that type and a cast is not a filter. No Plaid call was added and nothing new is billed. WHAT REMAINS OPEN AND IS NARROWER THAN THIS ITEM STARTED: whether /accounts/balance/get is wired for a household asking whether something will clear right now, which is a different question with a different freshness requirement and a per-call cost justified by being asked. Cash Flow does not need it.

item: THE ABORTABILITY BOUNDARY, STATED RATHER THAN ASSERTED (Guy, 21 Aug 2026). A DEADLINE IS ONLY SAFE IF EVERY OPERATION UNDER IT IS GENUINELY ABORTABLE, so here is which operations in the sync path are and which are not. ABORTABLE AND NOW BOUNDED: every outbound Plaid call, because callPlaid passes an AbortController signal to fetch and a 30 second per-call timer aborts it. NOT ABORTABLE AND NOT BOUNDED: every database operation. runSyncForItem opens postgres(databaseUrl, { max: 1 }) with no connect_timeout, no idle_timeout and no statement_timeout, and nothing carries a signal, so A HUNG QUERY INSIDE THE TRANSACTION IS UNBOUNDED AND HOLDS THE HOUSEHOLD'S CHAIN LOCK FOR AS LONG AS IT HANGS. That is the same failure the Plaid deadline was built to prevent, on the other half of the same critical section. ALSO NOT BOUNDED, and smaller: the Durable Object fetch that takes the lock, and the service-binding fetches from api to sync, none of which pass a signal. decryptToken is CPU-bound WebCrypto and cannot meaningfully hang. CLOSED FOR THE DATABASE HALF 21 AUG 2026 by migration 0031, ALTER ROLE marginsheet_sync SET statement_timeout = 30s, with the value derived from a real production run and the figures in the migration. The Durable Object fetch and the service-binding fetches remain unbounded and are smaller. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: no hung query has been observed. Neon is a managed service and the sync's statements are small and indexed. This is a gap in the guarantee rather than a live incident, and it is recorded because the guarantee was about to be described as if it covered the whole operation. THE LIKELY SHAPE OF THE FIX is a statement_timeout on the sync role's connection rather than a signal, since Postgres bounds statements natively and the client-side abort of a query in flight is not reliably a cancellation. That is a different mechanism from the Plaid deadline and wants its own ruling on the value.

item: LIABILITY_DETAILS HAS A CONSUMER, A GRANT AND A CONSENT, AND NO WRITER. `last_statement_balance` paired with `next_payment_due_date` is Cash Flow's committed outflow: a known amount on a known date, which is why it renders as committed rather than estimated (Guy, 21 Aug 2026). IT IS THE REASON THE CARDS WERE CONNECTED. The table exists from 0002, `marginsheet_sync` has held grants on it since 0023, and `liabilities` is declared in config/plaid-consent.json as an additionally-consented product. item: WHAT THE FIRST RECONCILIATION OUTPUT WILL MEAN, DECIDED BEFORE THE DATA ARRIVES (Guy, 21 Aug 2026). Webhooks are live on all three institutions, nine pending rows existed when this was written, and transactions.settled_at records the pending-to-posted transition, so the first settle and the first non-zero difference are plausibly the same event. THE HEALTHY CASE: settleCriterion reports discharged, and a non-zero difference appears on the same account IN ONE OBSERVATION AND IS ZERO ON THE NEXT. That is a settle moving the reported balance without moving the created_at sum, the baseline then absorbing it, and it requires no action: the acceptance criterion open since 17 Aug discharges and the reconciler is behaving as designed. THE CASE THE WINDOW EXISTS FOR: a non-zero difference that PERSISTS across intervals, meaning every interval brings a fresh disagreement rather than one event seen repeatedly. THAT IS NOT A SETTLE and the response is to stop and diagnose rather than to wait: candidates are transactions we never receive, a fee or interest the institution applies outside the transaction feed, a removed row mishandled, or a sign wrong for an account type. THE THIRD CASE, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT WOULD BE MISREAD: a non-zero difference on a CREDIT account that persists while depository accounts stay clean. That is the sign inversion, and it would look like an institution problem. Check expectedBalance before checking Plaid. WHY THIS IS WRITTEN DOWN NOW: a reading decided after the data exists is a reading the data helped choose, and the first alert will arrive unattended. AND "NO DRIFT OBSERVED" IS NOT CITABLE, for a stronger reason than a quiet run (Guy, 21 Aug 2026). EVERY ACCOUNT HOLDS EXACTLY ONE SNAPSHOT, ALL DATED 2026-08-21. There has never been a second observation to compare against, so no interval has ever been measured and the reconciler has never had the inputs its verdict requires. That is not the same as a run that wrote nothing, which merely fails to add evidence: this says no evidence of the kind has ever existed. The criterion sits looking green because a first observation is correctly not a drift, and a column of first observations is indistinguishable from a column of clean ones.

item: THE WITHIN-ITEM HALF OF THE SCOPING DEFECT, AND IT SURVIVED THE FIX. Scoping reconciliation to the Item removed the cross-Item case: an account belonging to a needs_reauth Item is no longer judged inside a healthy Item's sync. IT DID NOT REMOVE THE SAME DEFECT ONE LEVEL IN. reconcileBalances evaluates every ACTIVE account of the Item, while applyBalances only refreshes accounts Plaid returned on a page, and /transactions/sync returns only accounts that HAVE TRANSACTIONS on that page. So a quiet account on a syncing Item is reconciled against a balance from an earlier moment, with no new transactions, and reconciles to zero: a measurement of nothing recorded as a passing observation, exactly as the cross-Item case was. AND A PASSING OBSERVATION IS NOT INERT, because the window confirms across three CONSECUTIVE non-zero differences and a zero breaks the run. THIS IS WHAT REMAINS OF FINDING 1 AND IT IS NOT THE COUNTER. Item 1 reporting balanceWritesIssued 1 while producing eighteen reconciliation verdicts was comparing two tables: balance writes count account_balance_snapshots upserts, reconciliation rows are balance_reconciliations, and no counter has ever claimed the second. The mismatch that remains is between ACCOUNTS RECONCILED and ACCOUNTS WHOSE BALANCE WAS READ, which is a real and different statement. THE FIX IS PROBABLY TO RECONCILE ONLY THE ACCOUNTS applyBalances TOUCHED, which run-sync already collects, and that would make the counter meaningful rather than cosmetic. Not built: it is beyond the scope approved for the scoping fix and it wants its own ruling. CLOSED by task 1b (#163): applyBalances returns the ids it refreshed, run-sync accumulates them across pages, and reconcileBalances judges only those. An unrefreshed account gets NO ROW rather than a row saying zero, and is reported with comparable false and a reason.

item: services/sync/src/outbox.ts IS IMPORTED BY NOTHING. markEnqueued, findRepairable and countNeverAnnounced have no caller in any src file, and their only references are tests. run-sync WRITES household_state_signals rows on every sync that changes something, and NOTHING EVER ANNOUNCES THEM: the signals accumulate with enqueued_at null forever. The consumer is the watcher in conversation-service-spec section 'The watcher', which is M13 and does not exist. So the design is ruled and only the transport is absent. plaid-pipeline-spec:105 is the sentence that makes waiting correct rather than merely cheap: 'a queue transport makes the thin payload do more work than an in-database outbox would', which states the in-database outbox as the legitimate resting position and the queue as the further-travelling one. WIRING IT NOW WOULD PUT ITS ONLY CONSUMER IN CI, which is the orphan lesson pointed the other way: markEnqueued would set enqueued_at against a queue nobody reads, and enqueued_at would stop meaning 'announced' and start meaning 'we said so'. ALLOWLIST ENTRY RETYPED 22 AUG 2026 rather than removed: outbox.ts stays declared in BUILT_AND_NOT_WIRED, now under reason 'consumer_does_not_exist_yet' naming M13 as the supplier. item: services/sync/src/sync-state.ts IS IMPORTED BY NOTHING, and there is NO CRON ON EITHER WORKER. sweepReason has twelve test references and zero callers; onWebhook has two and zero. The watchdog exists to distinguish a stuck sync from a slow backfill, which is the distinction 4.4 built last_cursor_at for and which CLAUDE.md records a whole finding about. IT HAS NEVER RUN. A sync that hangs stays sync_status = 'syncing' indefinitely and nothing sweeps it back, which is the exact condition the watchdog was written to end. THE TWELVE TEST REFERENCES ARE THE POINT: this is the most heavily tested function in the module and it is unreachable. Found 21 Aug 2026 alongside the liabilities fetcher, same shape. CORRECTED AND ENLARGED 22 AUG 2026. TWO ERRORS IN THE ORIGINAL WORDING. First, 'sync-state.ts is imported by nothing' is FALSE: run-sync.ts imports onSyncComplete and the SyncStatus type. The scan reported two FUNCTIONS with no caller and the item generalised to the MODULE, which is a larger claim than the evidence supported. SECOND AND MUCH WORSE: NOTHING ANYWHERE SETS sync_status TO 'syncing'. All three production Items read 'idle'. sweepReason's first line returns null unless the status is 'syncing', so A CRON ADDED TODAY WOULD RUN ON SCHEDULE, EXAMINE EVERY ITEM, SWEEP NOTHING FOREVER, AND REPORT HEALTHY. That is the failure this repository has named more than any other, and wiring the trigger alone would have built it. SO THE TASK IS NOT 'ADD A CRON', IT IS 'BUILD THE STATE MACHINE'S WRITE HALF': mark syncing at sync start, persist a start time, call onWebhook when a webhook lands mid-sync so the queued follow-up actually happens, and only then add the sweep and its trigger. onSyncComplete is called today and always receives 'idle', so its queued branch is unreachable too: THE STATE MACHINE HAS THREE FUNCTIONS, ONE CALLER, AND THAT CALLER ALWAYS GETS A VALUE THAT MAKES IT A NO-OP. Scope is materially larger than what was approved as 'wire the watchdog' and needs Guy's ruling before it is built. WRITE HALF BUILT 22 AUG 2026 under 4.8: the marker commits in its own transaction before the main one, sync_started_at lands in the same statement, onWebhook is called by the webhook handler so the queued branch is reachable, and sweepStuckSyncs resolves a stale syncing to 'swept' rather than idle. sweepReason and onWebhook now have callers and are out of the orphan allowlist. WHAT REMAINS IS THE TRIGGER, tracked as the-sweep-has-no-trigger-yet. CLOSED 22 AUG 2026. The trigger is a Cloudflare cron on the sync Worker, every ten minutes, declared PER ENVIRONMENT because named environments do not inherit top-level keys and this repo already has an incident about that. WORST-CASE TIME TO SWEEP IS THE 30 MINUTE THRESHOLD PLUS THE INTERVAL: 40 minutes, and the threshold dominates, which is why a faster cron buys almost nothing. Every run writes a sweep_runs row INCLUDING RUNS THAT SWEEP NOTHING, because a cron that stopped firing and a cron with nothing to do produce the same observable and the row is what separates them. The readout reports the trace's age and verify-deploy asserts it. NEITHER IS CONTINUOUS: a stopped cron is found the next time somebody deploys or looks, which is stated on the table rather than papered over, and closing it needs monitoring outside this stack.

item: reconnectItem AND markReconnected HAVE NO CALLER, while createLinkToken and itemProducts from the same module do. item: financial_accounts.liability_coverage DEFAULTS TO 'unknown' FOR EVERY ACCOUNT AND IS ONLY EVER WRITTEN FOR CREDIT ONES. fetch-liabilities scopes every write to type = 'credit' or to an account id returned in liabilities.credit[], so the six depository and two investment accounts in the founder household hold 'unknown' PERMANENTLY, meaning NOT APPLICABLE, while a card holding 'unknown' means NOT YET FETCHED. TWO FACTS, ONE VALUE, OPPOSITE REMEDIES: ignore it forever, or enable liabilities and sync. Cash Flow reads this column BEFORE reading last_statement_balance precisely so it can tell why a figure is missing, and this is the one distinction it cannot make. THE FIX IS A SPLIT RATHER THAN A NOTE, per the class recorded in CLAUDE.md the same night: either a fifth value 'not_applicable' written for non-credit accounts, or the column scoped so only credit accounts carry it at all. The second is cleaner and costs a migration plus a nullable column. WRITTEN BY SOMEONE WHO HAD SPENT THE EVENING NAMING THIS EXACT FAILURE IN THREE OTHER PLACES, which is the argument for the class being named rather than for more care. RULED 21 AUG 2026 (Guy): FIX IT WITH A STATE FOR NOT APPLICABLE, DISTINCT FROM unknown, before Cash Flow reads it. NOT DONE IMMEDIATELY, and the reason is mechanical rather than a judgement about urgency: Postgres will not let a new enum label be USED in the transaction that adds it, so this costs TWO migrations whenever it is done, one to add 'not_applicable' and one to backfill non-credit rows and to start writing it. Doing it today costs two and doing it with the M6b work costs two, so there is no saving, and the rows accumulating in the meantime are corrected by the same backfill either way. THE CONTROL THAT COMES WITH IT IS PER-INSTANCE AND THAT IS THE ONLY KIND AVAILABLE HERE: no credit account may hold 'unknown' once liabilities is enabled for its Item, and no non-credit account may hold anything but 'not_applicable'. Both are database tests. Neither generalises to the class, which is a review prompt rather than a control.

item: THE WATCHDOG'S PROGRESS BRANCH CANNOT FIRE, AND THE VALUE IT READS BELONGS TO A DIFFERENT RUN. sync-state.ts states its design content plainly: measure from LAST CURSOR PERSISTENCE rather than from sync start, because a 20,000 transaction backfill reads as stuck when measured from start and gets swept mid-flight. run-sync writes last_cursor_at PER PAGE BUT INSIDE THE MAIN TRANSACTION, so no cursor write is visible to anything until the whole sync commits, and at that moment the status is already idle. AN ITEM THAT IS 'syncing' HAS, BY CONSTRUCTION, NO COMMITTED CURSOR FROM THAT RUN. WORSE THAN INERT: the marker does not clear last_cursor_at, so a hung sync inherits the timestamp of the PREVIOUS SUCCESSFUL run, and the sweep declines to fire on evidence from work that already finished. The delay is bounded, it is measured from the wrong moment, and the progress it reads is another run's. THE TENSION IS REAL AND NEITHER HALF IS WRONG. One transaction gives the sync atomicity across streams, balances, reconciliation and liabilities, which is why it is one. Per-page persistence gives observable progress, which is why 4.4 built it. THEY ARE INCOMPATIBLE AS WRITTEN and nothing noticed because the branch needing the second has never run. TWO OPTIONS AND THE CHOICE IS A RULING ABOUT WHAT A SYNC GUARANTEES. (A) Persist the cursor in its own committed transaction per page, which makes progress observable and gives up atomicity between the cursor and the rows that page wrote: a crash could leave a cursor ahead of its transactions, which is the duplicate-import hazard the two-cursor design already exists to manage. (B) Accept a start-only watchdog, clear last_cursor_at when marking syncing so no stale value is read, and raise STALE_AFTER_MS above the longest plausible backfill, which sweeps a genuinely hung sync later and never cancels a working one. B IS CHEAPER AND WEAKER; A IS WHAT 4.4 INTENDED. Found 22 Aug 2026 by Guy asking where the completion write sits relative to the main transaction. The completion write is INSIDE it, so the gap he asked about (work committed, completion lost) cannot occur: they are atomic. The seam he pointed at was real and one level below where he pointed. RULED B AND DONE 22 AUG 2026. The progress branch, ItemSyncState.lastCursorAt and their tests are deleted; the threshold is start-only and derived; last_cursor_at keeps its data and its collapsed meaning is recorded on the column. Amendment 15.

item: STALE_AFTER_MS IS DERIVED RATHER THAN MEASURED AND IS OWED A RE-DERIVATION. 30 minutes comes from the only throughput ever recorded: SoFi's first sync, 1,560 transactions in 47 seconds, in migration 0031's comment. Amex's 5,241-row first sync is the largest observed and computes to 2.6 minutes at that rate, so 30 is a 10x multiple of the worst observed case and clears a hypothetical 20,000-row backfill with 3x headroom. NO SYNC HAS EVER BEEN TIMED END TO END, because until 4.8 nothing recorded a start. plaid_items.sync_started_at persists one now and the completion write is observable, so real durations accumulate from 22 Aug 2026 onward. Re-derive against the actual distribution once enough exist, and record the sample size beside the number, because a threshold with no stated basis is a number that explains itself falsely. N IS NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT FLOATING (Guy, 22 Aug 2026): FIFTY completed syncs carrying both a sync_started_at and a completion, ACROSS AT LEAST TWO ITEMS, INCLUDING AT LEAST ONE FIRST SYNC. The composition matters as much as the count: fifty incremental syncs on one Item would measure the cheap case fifty times and say nothing about the backfill this threshold exists to protect. IT IS PROSE-TYPED AND NOT CONDITION-TYPED, DELIBERATELY. The condition kinds this repo supports are path_exists, file_contains and control_exists, none of which can reach a database, so a count of completed syncs is not something the repo can evaluate. Typing it as a condition would be prose wearing a mechanism's label, which the open-items check refuses by design and which would be worse than leaving it prose.
trigger: 50 completed syncs carrying a sync_started_at and a completion, across at least 2 Items, including at least 1 first sync. Prose because no supported condition kind can query a database.

item: A STOPPED CRON IS FOUND AT NEXT DEPLOY-OR-LOOK, NOT WHEN IT STOPS. The watchdog's sweep writes a sweep_runs row on every run including empty ones, so a dead scheduler is distinguishable from a quiet one, and the trace's age is asserted by verify-deploy and reported by the ledger readout. NEITHER IS CONTINUOUS. Nothing in this system runs continuously except the cron itself, so the thing that would notice its absence is the thing that is absent. CONTINUOUS DETECTION NEEDS MONITORING OUTSIDE THIS STACK and is deliberately not built bespoke: it is the same family as the cyber liability quotes and the WISP, operational maturity that arrives with beta scale, and it should be bought once alongside uptime monitoring rather than assembled here. The trace is the half that has to exist first, because external monitoring needs something to watch and an endpoint reporting 'last sweep N minutes ago' is that something.

item: FOUND 22 AUG 2026 while deciding whether to build the announcer, which is why the announcer decision was worth taking to the spec. plaid-pipeline-spec section 4 rules SEVEN change kinds for household-state-changed: transactions_added, transactions_modified, transactions_removed, balances_updated, item_status_changed, recurring_updated, liabilities_updated. run-sync.ts writes THREE. AND THE GATE IS THE LARGER HALF: the whole insert sits behind didChange(outcome), which is `counts.added + counts.modified + counts.removed > 0` in apply-streams.ts:259, a pure function of the TRANSACTION stream. So a sync that refreshed balances, wrote snapshots, fetched liabilities and changed an Item's status, and added no transactions, FIRES NO SIGNAL AT ALL. The spec's rule is 'a sync that changed nothing does not fire'; the implementation is 'a sync whose TRANSACTIONS did not change does not fire', and those are the same sentence only for the input it was written against. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE ONE THE SPEC ITSELF NAMES AT LINE 103: 'building only the signal would leave those rules permanently silent'. The watcher's first-shipping rules are the balance, anomaly and price-change rules, and a balance-only sync would never wake it. NOTHING IS LOST TODAY, because the underlying rows are all in the database and nothing reads signals yet, so this is a notification gap rather than a data gap. It is recorded now rather than left for M13 because M4 owns the pipeline and the change kinds are legible here; discovered in M13 it would present as a watcher that never fires.
